series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 1/3] mm: swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a new folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator function. The current implementation adds the folio to the LRU immediately, which prevents callers from acting on the folio before it becomes visible for reclaim. This change is necessary for two use cases: refault evaluation and zswap writeback dropbehind. By deferring the LRU insertion to the callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(), there is no functional change intended, but rather a preparatory step for future changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 2/3] mm: swap: refault on swap-in, not in the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the evaluation of page refaults from the swap cache allocator to the two callers that perform swap-in operations. This change prevents inflated working set statistics when zswap writeback continuously writes back compressed data. The patch also ensures that the shadow is handed back correctly in the swap cache allocation function, and fixes a potential issue with stale snapshots being used for refault evaluation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 3/3] mm: zswap: preserve the workingset shadow across writeback
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue in the zswap compression algorithm where the workingset shadow is lost during writeback operations, leading to inaccurate anon refault/workingset accounting. To fix this, the patch preserves the workingset shadow within zswap by parking it in the zswap tree instead of overwriting it when allocating a new buffer folio. The parked shadow is then handled at the next opportunity, whether that's during swap-in, reclaim, or slot free operations.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series fixes a problem in the zswap writeback path where workingset refaults were being over-counted and eviction cookies were being lost, leading to inaccurate workingset detection. The patches preserve the shadow within zswap itself by parking the captured shadow in the zswap tree instead of erasing it when writing back to disk. This is done without introducing new swap-table or swap-slot state. As a result, refault evaluation is moved out of the swap-cache allocator and into the swap-in callers, preventing miscounted refaults. The patches were tested with a sysbench OLTP workload and showed significant reductions in workingset refaults, activations, and restores (-48%, -59%, and -53% respectively), while maintaining comparable writeback volume and unaffected throughput.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 3/3] btrfs: downgrade the reflink source inode lock for tree walking

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 3/3] btrfs: downgrade the reflink source inode lock for tree walking

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch downgrades the lock on the source inode during reflink operations from exclusive to shared, allowing other processes to access the file while a reflink is in progress. This improves performance by reducing stalls caused by concurrent clones and lseeks or dio reads on the src file. The patch also adds checks for direct IO writes that come in under EOF and ensures that the inode flag 'BTRFS_INODE_REFLINK_SRC' is visible to the dio writer. Additionally, it remains exclusive to dio reads through finishing the prep to prevent starving the clone on a stream of dio readers.

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 2/3] btrfs: skip unlocked reflink source flush if the inode has writers

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Btrfs reflink source flush behavior to skip the unlocked flushing if there are active writers dirtying pages. This is done by checking for outstanding writable file descriptors or memory mappings, which can cause redundant writeback. The change aims to reduce write amplification and user-space stalls in certain workloads, particularly those with long open file descriptors or continuous writes.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 1/3] btrfs: pre-flush reflink source before taking inode locks

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 1/3] btrfs: pre-flush reflink source before taking inode locks

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the reflink operation in Btrfs by pre-flushing the source file before taking inode locks, reducing contention between writers and readers. The current logic blocks concurrent usage of inode locks during writeback, leading to performance issues. This patch introduces an optimistic btrfs_wait_ordered_range() call without locks, relying on subsequent calls under locks for correctness. In case of concurrent writes while unlocked, the worst-case scenario is a redundant writeback, considered a reasonable trade-off for avoiding reader lock contention in common cases.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 0/3] reduce reflink src inode lock contention

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 0/3] reduce reflink src inode lock contention

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch reduces contention on the src inode lock during reflink operations by attempting to perform some writeback outside of the lock and downgrading the lock to shared when safe. The approach involves pre-flushing the source file before taking the locks, skipping flush if there are writers, and then downgrading the lock for tree walking. This should reduce contention on the src inode i_rwsem during reflink operations.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's /proc/PID/pagemap and /proc/PID/clear_refs functionality. The issue arises when a special PMD (Page Map Directory) is installed from a PFN (Physical Frame Number) that does not have a corresponding memmap entry. This causes the kernel to oops when trying to read or write these mappings. To fix this, the patch uses vm_normal_folio_pmd and vm_normal_page_pmd functions instead of pmd_folio and page_folio in certain paths, allowing the kernel to handle special PMDs correctly. The patch has been tested on QEMU with a test driver and has been reported to resolve the issue.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] mm/madvise: reclaim isolated folios if PTE restart fails

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/madvise: reclaim isolated folios if PTE restart fails

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a concurrency issue in the Linux kernel's madvise functionality. When MADV_PAGEOUT is used to collect isolated folios, a concurrent operation can remove or replace the PTE table while the lock is dropped, causing pte_offset_map_lock() to return NULL and bypassing reclaim_pages(). The patch routes this failure through the existing cleanup path, ensuring that any collected folios are reclaimed or put back. This fix prevents a situation where isolated folios remain off the LRU with elevated references.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 0/5] nfsd/sunrpc: allow userland to handle rpcbind registration

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 0/5] nfsd/sunrpc: allow userland to handle rpcbind registration

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 1/5] SUNRPC: allow a service to opt out of rpcbind registration
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows a service to opt out of rpcbind registration by introducing a new flag, sv_no_rpcbind, in the svc_serv structure. When this flag is set, the service will not be registered with rpcbind and the corresponding code paths are updated to honor this flag. This change does not affect any existing behavior as no caller has yet set this flag.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 2/5] NFSD: add a userspace-rpcbind flag to listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new 'userspace-rpcbind' flag to the listener_set interface, allowing callers to take over rpcbind registration from the kernel. The flag is echoed in the reply when accepted by the kernel, and the caller must not change ownership while a server exists. The patch also updates the netlink specification to include this new flag and its associated attributes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 3/5] NFSD: honour the userspace-rpcbind flag in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD listener_set function to honour the userspace-rpcbind flag. When this flag is set, the kernel will not make an rpcbind call and instead sets sv_no_rpcbind on the service. This prevents synchronous rpcbind RPCs under nfsd_mutex and avoids issues with ownership changes. The legacy portlist add-fd interface also refuses to run against a service with this flag set. The patch affects several files in the NFSD codebase, including nfsctl.c, nfsd.h, and nfssvc.c.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 4/5] NFSD: report registerable programs in the listener_set reply
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) to report registerable programs in the listener_set reply when a caller owns rpcbind. The reply includes the programs and versions that nfsd would have registered, as well as the listeners to register them for. This information is sent only when the request asked for it, preserving compatibility with older callers. The patch also removes unnecessary code and optimizes memory allocation for large listener sets.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 5/5] selftests/nfsd: exercise the userspace-rpcbind listener_set flag
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds self-tests to the NFS daemon (nfsd) that exercise its interaction with the userspace rpcbind service, specifically covering the listener_set flag and various scenarios related to registration, ownership, and teardown of listeners.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series allows userland to handle rpcbind registration for nfsd listeners, adding a new optional flag to the netlink downcall that tells the kernel to skip rpcbind registration. The patches also include changes to exempt an empty listener list from the rpcbind ownership check and drop dead nfsacl test in nfsd_version_registerable().

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH fstests] btrfs: test graceful ENOMEM handling in synchronous dirops

version_history.subject: [PATCH fstests] btrfs: test graceful ENOMEM handling in synchronous dirops

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch adds a test case to the fstests suite to verify that Btrfs handles ENOMEM errors gracefully in synchronous directory operations. The test uses fault injection knobs to simulate an -ENOMEM error in the btrfs_prealloc_delayed_dir_index() function and checks that the filesystem remains consistent after the operation. The patch also introduces helper functions for driving the kernel's fail_function interface, which is used for fault injection.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 00/11] mountd: bugfixes for up/downcall interfaces

version_history.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 00/10] mountd: bugfixes for up/downcall interfaces

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 01/11] mountd: factor out the per-path export attribute computation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the computation of per-path export attributes in the mountd service to make it more modular and reusable. The patch introduces a new function `export_attrs_build` that takes an export path and an export entry as input and returns a struct containing the computed export attributes. This function is used by both the upcall and downcall paths, making it easier to manage cross-mount subdirectories and re-exported filesystems. No functional changes are made, only code organization improvements.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 02/11] mountd: handle unmountable paths and junctions in the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the handling of unmountable paths and junctions in the netlink downcall by nfsd_export(). It introduces a new function to check for junctions before denying exports, and splits the lookup_nonexport() function so that both downcalls can share the junction lookup. The patch also adds support for deferred requests, which are retried from cache_process() every RETRY_SEC seconds. This allows the kernel to keep the upcall pending in the meantime, improving performance and reliability.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 03/11] mountd: answer requests the kernel rejects on the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to handle rejected requests from the kernel due to failed filehandle construction or other issues. When a request is rejected, it resubmits each entry individually and answers negative for any entries that are still refused by the kernel. This approach prevents pending requests from piling up and allows clients to recover from failures more efficiently.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 04/11] mountd: don't leak the parent export's fsid onto crossmnt submounts
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the mountd service where cross-mount submounts inherit their parent's fsid, leading to incorrect filehandles and ESTALE errors on clients. The patch uses export_attrs_build() to compute the flags, fsid, and uuid for each export, masking per-flavor secinfo flags as needed. It also honors the export's own e_ttl on positive entries and falls back to a negative entry when an export cannot be resolved.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 05/11] mountd: retry unresolvable fsid lookups on the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to retry unresolvable file system ID (fsid) lookups on netlink downcalls. The fsid lookup is moved out of nfsd_handle_fh() and into a separate function, lookup_fsid(), which returns one of three possible values: FSID_LOOKUP_ANSWER (definitive), FSID_LOOKUP_RETRY (not resolvable yet), or FSID_LOOKUP_IGNORE (unusable). If the fsid lookup fails initially, it is added to a list of deferred netlink requests and retried on the same cadence as pipefs requests. This change helps prevent spurious ESTALE errors when the filesystem becomes available soon after the initial lookup failure.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 06/11] mountd: bound the junction path before copying it into e_path
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a potential heap corruption issue in the mountd service by bounding the junction path before copying it into e_path. The problem arises when a junction path exceeds NFS_MAXPATHLEN bytes, causing the strcpy function to write beyond the bounds of the fixed-size buffer. To prevent this, the patch checks the length of the junction path and rejects it if it's too long, returning NULL instead.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 07/11] mountd: give each worker its own netlink command socket
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where multiple workers in the mountd process share the same netlink command socket, leading to incorrect sequence checks and potential data corruption. To fix this, each worker is given its own netlink command socket by reopening the inherited sockets in the child processes. This ensures that each worker has its own reply stream and prevents two workers from taking each other's acknowledgments or error messages during a round trip.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 08/11] mountd: retry export attributes that fail to resolve for a passing reason
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to retry export attributes that fail to resolve due to a passing reason, such as a temporary error or an inability to determine whether a path is exportable. The patch introduces a new return value of EAGAIN for cases where the decision cannot be made immediately, and keeps EINVAL for genuine errors. This change allows the mountd service to recover from temporary issues and improve its ability to handle re-exported NFS mounts.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 09/11] mountd: drop a deferred fsid lookup once it has been answered
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service in the NFS-utils package to remove a deferred file system ID (fsid) lookup once it has been answered. The patch addresses an issue where an entry that resolves for the second time is still processed by nl_retry_expkey(), resulting in duplicate answers. To fix this, the patch introduces two new functions: delayed_expkey_matches() and delayed_expkey_remove(). The first function checks if a deferred fsid lookup matches a given request, while the second function removes any matching deferred lookup from the queue. The patch also updates the nl_expkey_singly() function to remove answered entries from the retry queue.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 10/11] mountd: bound the retry queues
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the size of three retry queues in the mountd service to prevent them from growing indefinitely. The queues are used when the server cannot immediately determine whether a client's filehandle is exportable, and they can be reached by clients through network requests. By capping these queues at MAX_DELAYED (1024 entries), the patch prevents excessive memory usage and latency caused by repeated deferrals. The cap only applies to new queue entries, allowing existing records to be re-queued without being dropped.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v3 11/11] mountd: don't warn about pipefs submounts nobody asked to export
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to stop issuing warnings when it encounters a submount that is not explicitly exported by an administrator. The change ensures that only paths that are being actively exported receive warnings, rather than all cross-mounts, which can lead to excessive and unactionable warnings.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses several bugs and issues in the mountd interface of the nfs-utils package, specifically related to up/downcall interfaces. The patches fix problems reported by Mantas, Sashiko, and others, including warnings about internal events, unexportable paths, and submounts nobody asked to export. The changes also include cleanup of warning messages, retrying transient failures, dropping deferred requests, and bounding junction path lengths. Overall, the patch series aims to improve the stability and reliability of the mountd interface.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the export_attrs_build() function in cache.c, which was previously handling crossmnt submounts and exported paths differently. The author moved the logic to adjust export flags, fsid, and uuid before handing them to the kernel into export_attrs_build(), making it consistent for both upcall and downcall paths.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about nfsd_export() handling errors from is_mountpoint(), which can fail with a strange error, leaving the path's exportability uncertain. The author agreed to restructure in v2 by deferring requests and retrying them later, using a new nl_add_export_req() function that handles both downcalls.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the batched SET_REQS message in mountd being dropped when the kernel rejects it, leading to pending requests piling up and client hangs on lookup. The author explained that they will resubmit each entry one at a time when the kernel rejects it, answer negative for entries still refused by the kernel, and log size failures instead of blaming the filesystem.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the nfsd_nl_add_export() function, which was sending e_flags and e_fsid from the parent exportent without stripping NFSEXP_FSID when the upcall path is a submount below the exported one. The author explained that this caused issues with re-exporting submounts via fsidnum and added code to use export_attrs_build() for flags, fsid, and uuid, masking per-flavor secinfo flags and falling back to a negative entry when the export cannot be resolved.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: Author addressed a concern about junction path length, explaining that the copy operation in create_junction_exportent() can lead to heap corruption if the path is too long. They proposed rejecting the path instead and added bounds checking to prevent this issue.
review_comments.raw_body:
create_junction_exportent() strcpy()s the junction pathname into
exportent.e_path, a fixed char[NFS_MAXPATHLEN+1].  Neither downcall
bounds the path first:

 - nfsd_export() sizes it from the 32KiB pipefs channel buffer
 - the netlink path strdup()s it out of NFSD_A_SVC_EXPORT_PATH

A junction more than NFS_MAXPATHLEN bytes deep therefore corrupts the
heap.  Reaching it needs a trusted.junction.nfs xattr, so only server
root can set one up, but the copy should not depend on that.

Reject the path instead, as mkexportent() already does.  The callers
handle a NULL exportent: both downcalls answer negative.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
Assisted-by: LLM
---
 support/export/cache.c | 6 ++++++
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)

diff --git a/support/export/cache.c b/support/export/cache.c
index 79dd0abe9a1b..6a5cdd9d9670 100644
--- a/support/export/cache.c
+++ b/support/export/cache.c
@@ -3434,6 +3434,12 @@ static struct exportent *create_junction_exportent(struct exportent *parent,
 {
 	static struct exportent *eep;
 
+	if (strlen(junction) >= sizeof(eep->e_path)) {
+		xlog(L_ERROR, "%s: junction path %s too long", __func__,
+		     junction);
+		return NULL;
+	}
+
 	eep = (struct exportent *)malloc(sizeof(*eep));
 	if (eep == NULL)
 		goto out_nomem;

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the handling of unresolvable fsid lookups in the netlink downcall, explaining that they should be retried instead of cached as negative. They moved the fsid lookup out of nfsd_handle_fh() into a new function lookup_fsid(), which returns an enum indicating whether to answer or retry. The author also explained how deferred netlink requests are handled and how rejected batches are resubmitted one entry at a time.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about shared netlink command sockets being used by multiple workers, which can lead to incorrect answers and client paths being marked as exported or negatively cached. The author explained that the current implementation shares one fd for every worker, but each worker should have its own reply stream. To fix this, the author will reopen both command sockets in the worker child, ensuring each worker gets its own reply stream.
review_comments.raw_body:
cache_open() opens the nfsd and sunrpc command sockets before
cache_fork_workers() forks, so every worker shares one fd, and a
copy-on-write struct nl_sock carrying the same s_seq_next/s_seq_expect.
Only the notify sockets get nl_socket_disable_seq_check(); the command
sockets keep libnl's default sequence check, which each worker will
happily pass on the other's reply.

Two workers in a command/reply round trip can therefore take each other's
ack or NLMSG_ERROR.  cache_nl_set_reqs() then reports the wrong outcome
and the caller answers the wrong client and path - marking it exported,
retryable, or negatively cached.

Reopen both command sockets in the worker child.  genl_connect() binds a
fresh port id, so each worker gets its own reply stream.  The notify
sockets stay shared: they are receive-only, have the sequence check
disabled, and are nonblocking, so whichever worker gets there first takes
the notification.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
Assisted-by: LLM

 support/export/cache.c | 37 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++--
 1 file changed, 35 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/support/export/cache.c b/support/export/cache.c
index 6a5cdd9d9670..cbe3df83b0eb 100644
--- a/support/export/cache.c
+++ b/support/export/cache.c
@@ -3994,6 +3994,29 @@ cache_wait_for_workers(char *prog)
 	}
 }
 
+/*
+ * Replace a command socket inherited across fork().  Returns @old if a new one
+ * cannot be had; sharing it is worse than having one, but not by as much as
+ * having none.
+ */
+static struct nl_sock *nl_cmd_sock_reopen(struct nl_sock *old)
+{
+	struct nl_sock *sock;
+
+	if (!old)
+		return NULL;
+
+	sock = nl_sock_setup();
+	if (!sock) {
+		xlog(L_WARNING, "%s: cannot reopen netlink command socket,"
+		     " sharing the inherited one", __func__);
+		return old;
+	}
+
+	nl_socket_free(old);
+	return sock;
+}
+
 /* Fork num_threads worker children and wait for them */
 int
 cache_fork_workers(char *prog, int num_threads)
@@ -4015,12 +4038,22 @@ cache_fork_workers(char *prog, int num_threads)
 		if (pid == 0) {
 			/* worker child */
 
+			/*
+			 * A command socket carries a reply back to the process
+			 * that sent the request, so it cannot be shared.  Every
+			 * worker inherits the same fd and the same copied
+			 * sequence counters, and two of them mid-round-trip
+			 * will take each other's ack.
+			 */
+			nfsd_nl_cmd_sock = nl_cmd_sock_reopen(nfsd_nl_cmd_sock);
+			sunrpc_nl_cmd_sock =
+				nl_cmd_sock_reopen(sunrpc_nl_cmd_sock);
+
 			/*
 			 * cache_open() drains the netlink downcalls before we
 			 * get here, so anything it deferred is now on the retry
 			 * queues of every worker.  Let the first worker own
-			 * those, or they get answered once per worker over the
-			 * shared command socket.
+			 * those, or they get answered once per worker.
 			 */

 				delayed_export_flush();

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the handling of statfs errors in export_attrs_build(), explaining that some errors, such as ETIMEDOUT or EIO, indicate that the path is not currently exportable but may be later, and therefore should return EAGAIN instead of EINVAL. The author also clarified that ENOSYS and 0 errors are handled differently.
review_comments.raw_body:
export_attrs_build() answers -1 both for a filesystem that can never be
exported and for one it could not measure this time:

 - nfsd_path_statfs() on a re-exported NFS mount can give ETIMEDOUT with
   "softerr", or EIO with plain "soft"
 - fsidnum_get_by_path() returns the same false whether fsidd is
   restarting, answered with nonsense, or has no fsid for the path

Both then set errno to EINVAL, so both downcalls deny the path for
default_ttl.  An fsidd restart takes a working re-export offline until the
negative entry expires.

Report EAGAIN for the cases we cannot decide and keep EINVAL for the rest.
The netlink path turns EAGAIN into EXPORT_RETRY, and nfsd_export() leaves
the request for the next upcall, which is what both already do when
is_mountpoint() fails oddly.

statfs errors are sorted with path_lookup_error(), the same test
is_mountpoint() callers use, plus two that are decidable even though it
does not name them:

 - ENOSYS: a filesystem with no statfs will never answer
 - 0: a chrooted worker thread ran the stat and its errno never reached
   us, which is how the is_mountpoint() callers already read it

Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
Assisted-by: LLM
---
 support/export/cache.c | 41 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
 1 file changed, 38 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/support/export/cache.c b/support/export/cache.c
index cbe3df83b0eb..290ce09bb66e 100644
--- a/support/export/cache.c
+++ b/support/export/cache.c
@@ -1145,7 +1145,9 @@ struct export_attrs {
  * it must not inherit the parent's fsid= or uuid= - if it does, both end up
  * claiming the same filehandles and the client sees ESTALE.
  *
- * Returns 0, or -1 with errno set if @path cannot be exported at all.
+ * Returns 0, or -1 with errno set: EAGAIN if we could not work the attributes
+ * out this time and the caller should ask again, anything else if @path is
+ * genuinely not exportable.
  */
 static int export_attrs_build(struct export_attrs *ea, char *path,
 			      struct exportent *exp)
@@ -1161,8 +1163,24 @@ static int export_attrs_build(struct export_attrs *ea, char *path,
 		struct statfs st;
 
 		if (nfsd_path_statfs(path, &st)) {
+			int err = errno;
+
 			xlog(L_WARNING, "unable to statfs %s", path);
-			errno = EINVAL;
+			/*
+			 * A strange error - the ETIMEDOUT a "softerr" NFS
+			 * re-export gives, or the EIO a plain "soft" one gives
+			 * - leaves us unable to say whether the path is
+			 * exportable, so ask again later.  Two errors are not
+			 * of that kind: ENOSYS, because a filesystem with no
+			 * statfs will never answer, and 0, which means a
+			 * chrooted worker thread ran the statfs and we never
+			 * saw its errno - is_mountpoint() callers read that as
+			 * definitive too.
+			 */
+			if (err != 0 && err != ENOSYS && !path_lookup_error(err))
+				errno = EAGAIN;
+			else
+				errno = EINVAL;
 			return -1;
 		}
 
@@ -1179,7 +1197,13 @@ static int export_attrs_build(struct export_attrs *ea, char *path,
 		if (exp->e_reexport != REEXP_NONE &&
 		    reexpdb_fsidnum_by_path(path, &search_fsidnum,
 			    exp->e_reexport == REEXP_AUTO_FSIDNUM) == 0) {
-			errno = EINVAL;
+			/*
+			 * fsidnum_get_by_path() answers the same way whether
+			 * fsidd is unreachable, gave us nonsense, or has no
+			 * fsid for this path.  A restarting fsidd must not
+			 * deny a working re-export, so ask again later.
+			 */
+			errno = EAGAIN;
 			return -1;
 		}
 		ea->fsidnum = search_fsidnum;
@@ -1845,6 +1869,10 @@ static enum export_result nl_add_export_req(struct nl_msg *msg, char *dom,
 	}
 
 	if (epp && export_attrs_build(&ea, path, epp) < 0) {
+		if (errno == EAGAIN) {
+			res = EXPORT_RETRY;
+			goto out;
+		}
 		xlog(explicit_export ? L_WARNING : D_GENERAL,
 		     "Cannot export %s, possibly unsupported"
 		     " filesystem or fsid= required", path);
@@ -3637,6 +3665,13 @@ static void nfsd_export(int f)
 				      NULL, 60);
 		} else if (dump_to_cache(f, buf, sizeof(buf), dom, path,
 					 &found->m_export, 0) < 0) {
+			/*
+			 * We could not work out the attributes this time.
+			 * Leave the request for the next upcall rather than
+			 * denying an export that is probably fine.
+			 */
+			if (errno == EAGAIN)
+				goto out;
 			xlog(L_WARNING,
 			     "Cannot export %s, possibly unsupported filesystem"
 			     " or fsid= required", path);

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] fuse: don't drop destination page cache on a zero byte copy reply

version_history.subject: [PATCH] fuse: don't drop destination page cache on a zero byte copy reply

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace) kernel module where it incorrectly drops the destination page cache when the server replies that no bytes were copied during a copy_file_range operation. The issue occurs when the source file is shorter than the size cached by the kernel, causing the end of the range to be -1 and resulting in all folios being dropped from the destination mapping. The patch adds a check for zero byte copies and only clears the cache if bytes were actually copied.
